title: An Experimental Study of the Performance of Wheat and Corn Straw Ash Cementitious Composite Materials
content: A new type of construction material is mainly introduced in this study, exploring the flowability, mechanical properties, dry density, and economic feasibility of wheat and corn straw fiber cementitious composite (WCSFCC) to produce high-pressure bricks. WCSFCC is developed to utilize wheat and corn straw fiber resources to replace the sand in conventional concrete bricks. The findings show that adding straw ashes to the straw fiber cement-based mixture improved the compressive strength from 11.48 MPa to 19 MPa at 28 days of age, while the flexural strength of WCSFCC was raised to 7.0 times at 28 days. Meanwhile, investigating the impact of straw ash dosage on trial outcomes revealed that 5 wt% straw ash satisfies the standard criteria for non-load-bearing and load-bearing wall structures. The dosing of straw ash changes and optimizes the WCSFCC structure, making the samples lighter and lower density. In addition, from the perspective of economic feasibility and sustainable development, it is more beneficial to the environment and health.
